overview: Transformer Health and Replacement Priority addresses telemetry is noisy or missing, so operators spend time interpreting unrelated warnings in power and utilities operations. The first proof of value uses oil test results, thermal loads and asset age. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is critical transformer failures, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: oil test results, thermal loads and asset age; define critical transformer failures and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Grid Operations Director / Chief Asset Officer.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including inject sensor failures, stale data and dependency loss into the pilot.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
